吴姜在群里跟大郎、二愣子和三狗子扯了足足半个多小时，答应给大朗邮寄几张护身符之后，这才退出了群聊。

该办正事了，吴姜将意识沉入阴差令牌，点开了兑换中心。

兑换中心的界面清晰明了，各类商品按品类划分得整整齐齐，术法、法器、丹药、符箓应有尽有，看得吴姜眼花缭乱。

第一个看的就是《纸鹤寻引术》，上次见玄丰道长使用之后，他就下定决心兑换了。

这门术法标价一百贡献点，和之前他买的《茅山基础符箓大全》价格一样，属于基础法术的范畴，同样是茅山有偿提供给地府的。

这门术法会的门派不少，属于大路货色，而且术法效果很单一，就是用符纸叠出一只灵鹤，注入一丝灵气后，便能循着邪祟散发的阴气，精准追踪其踪迹。

但不可否认，它的实用性极强。

“茅山和地府的关联，果然不是一般的深。”吴姜暗自嘀咕，目光扫过术法列表，发现大半术法都标注着“茅山提供”的字样。

除此之外，他还看到了崂山派、闾山派等道教大派的术法，吴姜看了看，龙虎山提供的没有几样，他眼馋的雷法，兑换中心里也没有。

吴姜稍一思索便想通了，龙虎山主要是混“上面”的，和茅山、崂山等这些门派不同，他们基本都是混“下面”的。

吴姜意识一点，直接兑换了《纸鹤寻引术》，一股信息流涌入了脑海，正是纸鹤寻引术的修炼方法，里面还包含了折纸鹤的技术。

紧接着，又花了五百贡献点，兑换了一个罗盘法器。

罗盘名字起的很霸气，苍龙盘，通体黝黑，盘面刻着密密麻麻的复杂纹路，边缘镶嵌着细碎的铜片，看着不起眼，用途却多了，可以定方位、测风水吉凶、寻龙点穴、探鬼寻阴，堪称道士的必备法器。

吴姜拿在手里细细把玩了一会儿，感受着罗盘上淡淡的灵气波动，便将它收进了阴差令牌。

罗盘别的功能他基本用不上，主要用的就是探鬼寻阴了。

搞定了抓鬼必备的两样必需品，吴姜才开始浏览其他商品。

先挑了两瓶辅助修炼的“聚阴丹”，丹药比基础术法还贵，两瓶就花了他一千贡献点，让他颇为肉疼。

Wu Jiang chatted with Dalang, Er Lengzi and San Gouzi in the group for more than half an hour, and then quit the group chat after promising to mail Dalang a few amulets.

When it was time to get down to business, Wu Jiang lowered his consciousness to the Yin Cha Token and opened the exchange center.

The interface of the exchange center is clear and clear, and all kinds of goods are neatly divided by category. There are all kinds of spells, magic weapons, elixirs, and talismans. Wu Jiang is dazzled by it.

The first thing I read was "Paper Crane Searching Technique". After seeing Taoist Master Xuanfeng use it last time, he made up his mind to redeem it.

This spell is priced at 100 contribution points, which is the same price as the "Maoshan Basic Talisman Encyclopedia" he bought before. It belongs to the category of basic spells and is also provided to the underworld for a fee by Maoshan.

There are many sects in this magic guild, and it belongs to the mainstream, and the magic effect is very simple. It is to use talisman paper to fold a spiritual crane, and after injecting a trace of spiritual energy, you can follow the evil spirit emitted and accurately trace its traces.

But it is undeniable that it is extremely practical.

"The connection between Maoshan and the underworld is really not that deep." Wu Jiang muttered to himself, scanning the spell list and found that most of the spells were marked with "Provided by Maoshan".

In addition, he also saw the magic techniques of major Taoist sects such as Laoshan Sect and Lushan Sect. Wu Jiang took a look and found that Longhu Mountain didn't offer many of them. The thunder method he was coveted was not available in the exchange center.

Wu Jiang thought for a while and figured out that Longhushan mainly belonged to the "upper level", unlike other sects such as Maoshan and Laoshan, which basically belonged to the "lower level".

Wu Jiang became more aware and directly redeemed the "Paper Crane Searching Technique". A stream of information poured into his mind. It was the training method of the Paper Crane Searching Technique, which also included the technique of origami cranes.

Immediately afterwards, he spent another 500 contribution points to exchange for a compass instrument.

The name of the compass is very domineering. It is a dark dragon disk with a dense and complex pattern carved on the surface. The edge is inlaid with fine copper pieces. It looks inconspicuous, but it has many uses. It can determine the direction, measure the good and bad fortune of Feng Shui, find the dragon's acupoints, and detect ghosts and find the underworld. It is a must-have magic weapon for Taoist priests.

Wu Jiang held it in his hand and played with it carefully for a while, feeling the faint spiritual energy fluctuations on the compass, and then put it into the Yin difference token.

He basically has no use for the other functions of the compass, and the main use is for detecting ghosts.

After getting the two necessities for catching ghosts, Wu Jiang started to browse other products.

First, he picked two bottles of "Yin Gathering Pills" to assist in training. The pills were more expensive than the basic spells. Two bottles cost him one thousand contribution points, which made him feel quite sad.
